verdicts.claim: The last connection to close a database runs one final checkpoint and then deletes the WAL file and the shared-memory wal-index file.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "that connection does one last checkpoint and then deletes the WAL and its associated shared-memory file"

verdicts.claim: Every new database connection has auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 pages (or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT); runs after commit on committing thread; all PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: wal_autocheckpoint: "defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages"; pragma: "All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE"; wal.html: "run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT"; pragma: "Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off.""

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE ... never invokes the busy handler. FULL ... blocks new writers but not readers. RESTART ... TRUNCATE truncates the WAL to zero bytes. NOOP...
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2 mode definitions match all five modes, e.g. TRUNCATE "truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return"

verdicts.claim: Every checkpoint takes an exclusive checkpoint lock; if another connection is checkpointing, returns SQLITE_BUSY without busy handler; FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE degrade to PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: "Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case"; "proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case"

verdicts.claim: Only a TRUNCATE checkpoint or a journal_size_limit (default -1, meaning no limit; checked at each WAL reset) reduces the file's on-disk size.
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: "The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)." and "Each time a transaction is committed or a WAL file resets, SQLite compares the size..."

verdicts.claim: Registering a custom callback with sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the built-in auto-checkpoint, and calling sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint() replaces any custom hook.
verdicts.evidence: "The callback registered by this function replaces any existing callback registered using sqlite3_wal_hook(). Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism"

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row with three integers ... C API returns the same counts through *pnLog and *pnCkpt, or -1 when not in WAL mode.
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: "returns a single row with three integer columns"; v2: "*pnLog is set to ... -1 if ... the database is not in WAL mode"

verdicts.claim: With synchronous=NORMAL, only checkpoints issue fsync, so moving checkpoints off the main thread removes sync stalls from it.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation"; "disable automatic checkpointing and run the periodic checkpoints in a separate thread, or separate process" (Syncthing source does not mention synchronous=NORMAL)

verdicts.claim: A forced TRUNCATE checkpoint waits for all active readers and holds the writer lock ... Litestream recommends truncate-page-n: 0 plus disk monitoring
verdicts.evidence: Litestream: "TRUNCATE checkpoints will block writes until all read transactions complete"; "Consider setting `truncate-page-n: 0` if your application has:" long-lived reads; disabling "Requires disk space monitoring and alerting"

verdicts.claim: Syncthing identified auto-checkpoint competing with app checkpointer as a cause of WAL starvation and proposed pool-release triggering
verdicts.evidence: "As checkpoints of any kind are exclusive, we're blocking our own checkpointer."; "Releasing a connection back to the pool would run our heuristic and invoke a checkpoint if needed." (thread dated 2026-02-06)
